text:
mike_infra: Heads up — since ~09:12 PT we're seeing intermittent DNS timeouts for internal service calls (model-agent -> config-service). A few retries then success, but increases job start latencies and some GPU jobs time out.

sara_sre: saw alerts too, paging spike for model-agent 5xx/timeouts. Any pattern by AZ or node pool?

mike_infra: looks cross-AZ. Error logs show: "dial tcp: lookup config-service.default.svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout". Pod-level nslookup inside same node works, but from different node in another AZ it intermittently fails.

jia_eng: can you paste netns dig from failing pod?

mike_infra: pasted minimal repro from failing pod:
```
# inside failing pod
> dig +short config-service.default.svc.cluster.local @10.96.0.10
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +short config-service.default.svc.cluster.local @10.96.0.10
; (1 server found)
; (waiting for response...)
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

oliver_net: interesting — node-local-dns (nodelocaldns) is returning NX for some queries while upstream CoreDNS shows no errors. Hypothesis: conntrack/NAT state getting exhausted on cross-AZ path causing UDP replies to be dropped, so node-local doesn't see answer.

sara_sre: conntrack? we've been seeing lots of short-lived UDP flows from autoscaling bursts recently. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion.

mike_infra: ran quick checks: `conntrack -S` shows entries jumping to ~300k on affected nodes; conntrack max is 262144 on those instances.

jia_eng: that would explain silence — return packets never make it back to the source port. When conntrack overflows kernel drops further states. Any packet loss counters?

oliver_net: tcpdump on node shows DNS responses arriving but with no matching conntrack entry for some of them. Also see ICMP unreachable messages from cross-AZ router briefly.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Notified net team channel and opened INC-2026-37 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-37)

squad-gpu-oncall: this is affecting GPU job startup (kubelet name resolution for imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent triggers extra lookups). Jobs are queuing and we have a backlog of ~12 pending GPU pods.

mike_infra: workaround applied: reduced DNS retry backoff in model-agent and enabled short-lived UDP conntrack timeout tuning on affected nodes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout=10` and increased `nf_conntrack_max` to 524288. Early signs: reduce timeouts on new requests.

sara_sre: we should be careful bumping conntrack_max without addressing root cause. Action items: 1) identify flow pattern causing high ephemeral UDP churn, 2) consider switching node-local-dns to TCP for internal queries across AZs, 3) add conntrack pressure alerts.

jia_eng: quick mitigation: patching node-local-dns config to prefer TCP for service lookups across AZ boundaries. Config snippet we used: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  stubDomains: |
    "default.svc.cluster.local":
      - 10.96.0.10
  upstreamProtocol: TCP
```
Note: YAML is pseudo — we toggled the resolver to force TCP for problematic paths.

oliver_net: long-term, net team will review cross-AZ path MTU and router logs; we saw earlier intermittent ICMP that could indicate MTU black-holing for fragmented UDP. If TCP works, that points to UDP frag/fragmentation or middlebox dropping.

mike_infra: agreed. Also we should throttle internal callers that do heavy churn (healthchecks every sec -> heavy DNS). Found a service doing tight DNS polling during startup. Asking owners to add a jitter/backoff.

sara_sre: created runbook entries:
- monitor conntrack entries per node
- alert when >70% usage for 5m
- escalate to net infra when ICMP spikes seen

squad-gpu-oncall: immediate status — backlog cleared to 3 pods after conntrack bump + node-local-dns TCP fallback. GPUs freed up, queue draining.

mike_infra: next steps: net team to share router/sr-iov logs, eng to audit services for DNS churn, infra to roll a safer conntrack increase across pools and add alerts. We'll update INC-2026-37 with timeline. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sara_sre: FYI adding a note to postmortem template that DNS timeouts can cascade into job provisioning pipeline (esp GPU pools).

jia_eng: follow-up: will instrument model-agent to cache lookups for 30s to reduce churn.

oliver_net: leaving traceroute/tcpdump capture running on 2 affected nodes for 24h. If anyone sees a recurrence, ping me first before rebooting nodes.

mike_infra: good call. closing thread when INC updated.
